name: Saltbone Numbers — The Shelf Daily Draw
description: The oldest continuously running illegal lottery in Meridian 88's Shelf districts, Saltbone Numbers uses a physical draw system — numbered bone chips pulled from a ceramic jar by a designated neutral party — specifically to avoid any digital interference or manipulation claims. Players buy numbered slips for Φ0.50 each, and daily draws happen at fixed locations in Shelf bars and canteens at 6pm. The operation has survived four major enforcement crackdowns by rotating its draw locations and burning its records daily.
story_hooks: The same number wins three consecutive daily draws — statistically impossible with fair bone-pull mechanics, suggesting either manipulation or something stranger.
A Saltbone runner is arrested carrying slips, but the arresting officer is more interested in the draw location list than the gambling charge — someone is hunting the network for a different reason.
A Φ1,800 jackpot winner is found dead before she can collect, and the slip has vanished — someone knew she'd won before the draw was announced.
